entities.text: frontlines of rapidly evolving crisis scenarios

nary_nodes.label: Google withdraws Earth AI tool
evidence: Google has rolled back its new AI tool that allowed people to create fake images on top of its satellite imagery

nary_nodes.label: Experts raise concerns about misuse and misinformation
evidence: experts raised concerns about misuse and the potential to spread misinformation

nary_nodes.label: Google announces AI image generator integration
evidence: the tech giant announced the integration of its AI image generator Nano Banana 2 into Google Earth

nary_nodes.label: Google states pausing feature for stronger guardrails
evidence: it said it was pausing the feature "while we work on implementing stronger guardrails"

nary_nodes.label: Google states users shared policy-violating screenshots
evidence: Google said it had seen "people sharing screenshots of generated imagery that appear to violate our policies"

nary_nodes.label: Retracted feature enables false scenario generation
evidence: The retracted feature enabled users to use text prompts to generate false scenarios on top of a base layer of real satellite, aerial or 3D imagery - which could then be downloaded and shared on other platforms.

nary_nodes.label: Google states people trust Google Earth for reliable view
evidence: "We know that people uniquely trust Google Earth for a reliable view of the world," it added.

nary_nodes.label: Experts state tool could spread misinformation
evidence: Experts told BBC Verify the tool could be used to spread misinformation with the appearance of Google's legitimacy - and highlighted the potential for bad actors to abuse it.

nary_nodes.label: BBC Verify creates fake images during testing
evidence: A collapsed Eiffel Tower, a sinkhole swallowing the Great Pyramid of Giza and Russian tanks in Ukraine's capital were among the images BBC Verify was able to create when testing the feature

nary_nodes.label: Henk van Ess highlights risks of fake image creation
evidence: AI and misinformation expert Henk van Ess highlighted the risks the feature posed, by creating fake images of a non-existent nuclear power plant in Iran, a refugee camp on the US-Mexico border and a fake hospital in Gaza with a bomb crater next to it.

nary_nodes.label: Henk van Ess states invented imagery welded to genuine coordinates
evidence: He said Google had allowed "invented" imagery to be "welded to genuine coordinates, drawn on genuine imagery".

nary_nodes.label: Henk van Ess states forgery inherits map credibility
evidence: "The forgery does not have to look convincing on its own. It inherits the credibility of the map it was born on," van Ess added.

nary_nodes.label: Google states AI content contains invisible watermarks
evidence: Google said AI content created by its tools contain invisible watermarks to indicate that they are fake or manipulated

nary_nodes.label: Google states users can check images with Gemini or Lens
evidence: anyone who is "unsure about an image" can check it using the Gemini chatbot app or use the Lens feature in its search.

nary_nodes.label: BBC Verify tests find watermarks effective
evidence: Generally, BBC Verify's tests found this is effective with images generated by the new feature.

nary_nodes.label: BBC Verify tests find watermarks circumnavigable
evidence: But we also found it was possible to circumnavigate these checks and trick Gemini into saying these fake Google Earth images are real.

nary_nodes.label: External AI detection tools fail to identify AI content
evidence: Tests using external AI detection tools also in some cases failed to identify the Google Earth AI-content.

nary_nodes.label: Henry Ajder states fake imagery in conflict zones destabilizing
evidence: AI-detection researcher Henry Ajder told BBC Verify the creation of fake imagery in conflict zones could prove particularly "destabilising" when events are fast-moving and information is scarce.

nary_nodes.label: Henry Ajder states not everyone will check images
evidence: "Journalists might be able to check that image… and report on it. But again, not everyone is going to do that," he added.

nary_nodes.label: Google initially stated guidelines prevent harmful topics
evidence: Google initially said that guidelines built into its AI model would prevent the creation of imagery depicting "harmful topics"

nary_nodes.label: BBC Verify found guidelines bypassable
evidence: BBC Verify found that small changes to prompts could be used to bypass these guidelines.

nary_nodes.label: Request to create 'raised platform' rejected
evidence: a request to create a "raised platform to hang traitors" next to the UK parliament was rejected.

nary_nodes.label: Image of 'raised platform' created with less specific prompt
evidence: But when a less specific prompt was used, it was accepted and the image was created.

nary_nodes.label: Request to mow 'Trump' into White House lawn rejected
evidence: We also asked the tool to mow the word "Trump" into the White House lawn, but it said it could not "create that image" based on its guidelines.

nary_nodes.label: Community garden generated in same spot
evidence: It did, however, allow a community garden to be generated in the same spot.

nary_nodes.label: Henry Ajder states unblemished spaces are valuable
evidence: spaces assumed to be "unblemished by AI are valuable, particularly for journalists and people trying to do work on the frontlines of rapidly evolving crisis scenarios"

nary_nodes.label: Henry Ajder states trusted information sources eroded by AI doubt
evidence: "It's concerning because it's another place where sources of trusted information are being eroded by the constant doubt that AI might be involved"

nary_nodes.label: Google Earth is entry point to satellite imagery
evidence: For many, Google Earth is the entry point to openly-accessible satellite imagery and can be used to obtain insights into hard to reach areas.

nary_nodes.label: Bill Greer states damage to public trust
evidence: "This is potentially particularly damaging to public trust because satellite imagery has historically been seen as an especially trustworthy source of data"

nary_nodes.label: Bill Greer states falsified satellite imagery used for misinformation
evidence: Falsified satellite imagery has already been used to spread misinformation, he added.

nary_nodes.label: Bill Greer states governments restricting data access
evidence: "Governments are also restricting access to data more and more, so we're likely to see more false images, and fewer real images which will further erode trust."
